content.title: About
content.content: Hard breadsticks are dry, crunchy snack sticks made from wheat flour, water, olive oil, and salt. They are commonly served in Italian restaurants and used as an accompaniment to sauces, soups, and salads. The texture is firm and crisp, while the flavor is mildly salty with a hint of olive oil.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Originally crafted in Italy, especially in the Tuscany and Lazio regions.
There are two main varieties: soft and hard. These sticks belong to the hard category.
In the United States they are often supplied to foodservice chains under the NFS (National Food Service) label.
Breadsticks can be flavored with garlic, rosemary, or sesame seeds.
They are considered a low‑calorie snack when not drenched in additional sauces.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Breadsticks contain starch that releases energy slowly, helping to maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with many snack foods, hard breadsticks typically contain only a small amount of fat.

items.title: Contains plant fiber
items.content: Dietary fiber supports normal digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Provides iron
items.content: The wheat flour used provides modest amounts of iron, which is important for blood formation.

items.title: Versatile with dips
items.content: Their crunchy texture makes them an excellent vehicle for tomato, cheese, or yogurt‑based dips, adding variety to the diet.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Made from wheat flour, they are unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Because of their high starch content, they can raise blood sugar quickly in individuals with diabetes.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Salt levels may be high; those monitoring sodium intake should limit portions.

items.title: Hard texture
items.content: The crunchy nature can be difficult to chew for young children or people with dental issues.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve as a snack alongside sauces, soups, or salads. Break into pieces and dip in olive oil with balsamic vinegar, tomato sauce, or cheese dip. Keep them dry to preserve crunch.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life, keep refrigerated to prevent oil from going rancid. Discard any sticks that develop mold odor or moisture.
